question: In the context of Gupta dynasty's administration, which of the following officers is **correctly **paired with their respective role?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pustapala-Notary and Keeper of Records**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Pustapala:** In the administration of the **Gupta dynasty**, the Pustapala was a **Notary** and **Keeper of Records**. They were responsible for maintaining important documents and administrative records, ensuring proper documentation and smooth functioning of governance. 
• **Utkhetayita:** This term refers to the **Keeper of the Royal Kitchen**, who oversaw all activities related to food preparation and supplies for the royal household. This designation was critical for maintaining the royal family's dietary needs.* (Incorrect pairing)* 
• **Dhruvadikaranika:** The term was associated with **Chief Judicial Officers** and was responsible for ensuring justice and legal order in the realm. Their role encompassed adjudicating disputes and upholding the king's law.* (Incorrect pairing)* 
• **Bhandagaradhikrita:** This officer was in charge of the **royal treasury** and not the **Head of Village Watchmen**. They ensured proper management of state funds and assets.* (Incorrect pairing)* 
• The correct answer highlights the accurate pairing of roles based on historical records of the **Gupta administration**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Gupta Dynasty Administration:** 
• The Gupta period (4th to 6th century CE) is regarded as a **golden age** of Indian history, with advancements in **art, science, literature, and administration.** 
• The Gupta administration was highly organized, with officers assigned specific roles to ensure efficient governance. 
• Prominent officers included **Kumaramatyas** (senior officials), **Mahadandanayaka** (chief judicial officers), and **Pustapala** (record keepers). 
• **Role of Pustapala:** 
• Pustapala played a vital role in maintaining administrative efficiency by ensuring that all royal decrees, land grants, and other important documents were systematically recorded. 
• Their work was instrumental in preserving historical records, which provide valuable insights into the Gupta period's governance and social structure. 
• **Hierarchy in Gupta Administration:** 
• Gupta administration was hierarchical, with the king at the top, followed by ministers, provincial governors, and local officers. 
• Each officer had a defined role, ensuring specialization and efficiency in governance. 
• **Historical Significance:** 
• The Gupta period's administrative structure influenced subsequent Indian kingdoms and is studied for its systematic and decentralized approach. 
• Records maintained by officers like the Pustapala have helped historians understand the socio-economic conditions of the time. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Gupta Land Grants:** 
• Land grants during the Gupta period were meticulously documented by officers like the Pustapala. These records were inscribed on copper plates and stone inscriptions. 
• Such grants often included tax exemptions and were issued for religious or charitable purposes, reflecting the socio-cultural priorities of the era. 
• **Economic Administration:** 
• The Gupta period saw a flourishing economy with advancements in trade, agriculture, and craftsmanship. 
• Officials like the Pustapala ensured proper documentation of economic transactions, which contributed to stable governance. 
• **Judicial and Military Organization:** 
• Gupta rulers maintained a balanced judicial and military system, with officers like **Mahadandanayaka** ensuring law and order. 
• The military was well-organized, with a focus on protecting the empire from external invasions. </ul
